summary:
Good morning. Here is today's Korean economic news briefing.

We begin with significant developments in Korea's economic policymaking structure. The newly appointed Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song met with Vice Premier and Minister of Economy and Finance Koo Yun-chul just four days after taking office. This meeting marks an important moment for economic coordination, as the two officials work to address mounting inflationary pressures stemming from the prolonged Middle East conflict. Governor Shin has signaled his commitment to price stability and financial market stability, while demonstrating a pragmatic approach that suggests the central bank will align with the government's expansionary fiscal stance. This represents a shift from past tensions between monetary and fiscal authorities over policy direction and institutional authority.

The Middle Eastern situation is creating tangible economic challenges for Korea. According to the Bank of Korea's latest data released yesterday, Korea's producer price index surged 1.6 percent month-over-month in March, marking the largest increase in four years. Year-over-year, producer prices climbed 4.1 percent, reflecting the dramatic spike in global oil prices. Most notably, petroleum product prices jumped approximately 30 percent. The Bank of Korea projects that raw material price increases will continue creating upward pressure on producer prices even as international oil prices have begun moderating from recent peaks. These cost pressures threaten to cascade through the economy, and consumer sentiment has deteriorated significantly, reaching its worst level since the martial law declaration. Consumers now expect inflation to rise 2.9 percent annually—a concerning 0.2 percentage point increase from the previous month.

Against this challenging backdrop, the government is emphasizing policy coordination and strategic investment. Yesterday, the Ministry of Economy and Finance hosted the 2026 Small and Medium Enterprise Technology Market AI Joint Forum in Sejong, bringing together over 400 participants from public institutions and private companies. Vice Minister Huh Jang underscored that artificial intelligence represents Korea's core national competitiveness in the contemporary era and stressed the government's commitment to policy and institutional support. The ministry announced the launch of a public sector AI utilization coordination body and promoted one-on-one matching consultations between AI suppliers and certified public institutions. These initiatives reflect the government's determination to accelerate the nation's digital transformation while building a robust artificial intelligence ecosystem spanning both public and private sectors.

The financial markets have shown resilience despite underlying economic headwinds. The KOSPI index closed yesterday at 6,417.93, gaining 29.46 points or 0.46 percent. More significantly, the KOSPI has achieved record highs after breaching the 6,400 level for the first time in Korean stock market history. The won-dollar exchange rate settled at 1,476 won per dollar, reflecting some modest currency volatility as investors navigate geopolitical uncertainties. Within the markets, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix continue attracting investor interest, driving strong demand for semiconductor-focused exchange-traded funds. Asset management companies have responded by launching new ETF products featuring these semiconductor giants, including bond-hybrid versions that combine equity exposure with safer fixed-income assets. The government has also signaled its intention to normalize government bond and public bond issuances in the second quarter, having reduced them in the first quarter to stabilize interest rates.

Real estate markets show mixed signals. High-end branded apartments are experiencing subscription competition rates approximately five times higher than general brand apartments, reflecting intensifying selectivity among consumers. Metropolitan Seoul apartment supply prices have risen 16.6 percent year-over-year as of March, reaching an average of 33.02 million won per 3.3 square meters. However, when adjusted for inflation, real residential property prices actually declined 1.66 percent year-over-year in the fourth quarter, with the contraction widening compared to the previous quarter. Meanwhile, the Korea Land and Housing Corporation announced it will recruit residents for rental-type affordable housing across 4,200 nationwide units, targeting newlywed couples, multi-child families, and new parents.

Internationally, developments in the Middle East and U.S. monetary policy are critical for Korea's economic outlook. The second round of peace negotiations between the United States and Iran collapsed, though a ceasefire remains in effect with extended terms. The U.S. Federal Reserve market remains focused on an upcoming confirmation hearing for the Fed chair candidate, with markets pricing in a 100 percent probability of a rate hold at the late April meeting. Meanwhile, American markets posted gains on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes reaching new highs as tensions eased momentarily. The Trump administration continues pursuing aggressive trade policies, with officials warning companies about tariff non-compliance in unmistakable terms.

Finally, the long-term implications of artificial intelligence deployment are drawing serious policy attention. Data center expansion for AI is projected to increase electricity demand by 26 percent by 2040, reaching 694.1 terawatt-hours annually. The Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power president emphasized that nuclear energy represents the most realistic solution for meeting this surging demand, highlighting the need to expand atomic energy's role with a focus on safety and cooperation. The government has committed to concentrated three-year investments in physical artificial intelligence capabilities that can supplement and replace human labor, even as private enterprises like Google Cloud report 40 percent quarter-over-quarter growth in enterprise AI users.

For investors and ordinary citizens, the economic landscape presents both opportunities and challenges. While equity markets have reached historic highs and technological investment remains robust, inflationary pressures from geopolitical disruptions demand caution. The May labor negotiations will prove critical in determining whether wage pressures will exacerbate inflation going forward. Policymakers are coordinating closely to maintain stability, but households should remain vigilant about price trends affecting daily essentials, particularly petroleum-based products and transportation costs. Long-term investors might consider infrastructure and energy companies benefiting from the AI-driven energy transition, while remaining mindful that real estate values are not keeping pace with nominal inflation.

This has been your Korean economic news briefing.
